1//! A cache containing data received from [`Shard`]s.
2//!
3//! Using the cache allows to avoid REST API requests via the [`http`] module where possible.
4//! Issuing too many requests will lead to ratelimits.
5//!
6//! # Use by Models
7//!
8//! Most models of Discord objects, such as the [`Message`], [`GuildChannel`], or [`Emoji`], have
9//! methods for interacting with that single instance. This feature is only compiled if the `model`
10//! feature is enabled. An example of this is [`Guild::edit`], which performs a check to ensure that
11//! the current user has the [Manage Guild] permission prior to actually performing the HTTP
12//! request. The cache is involved due to the function's use of unlocking the cache and retrieving
13//! the permissions of the current user. This is an inexpensive method of being able to access data
14//! required by these sugary methods.
15//!
16//! # Do I need the Cache?
17//!
18//! If you're asking this, the answer is likely "definitely yes" or "definitely no"; any in-between
19//! tends to be "yes". If you are low on RAM, and need to run on only a couple MB, then the answer
20//! is "definitely no". If you do not care about RAM and want your bot to be able to access data
21//! while needing to hit the REST API as little as possible, then the answer is "yes".
22//!
23//! [`Shard`]: crate::gateway::Shard
24//! [`http`]: crate::http
25//! [Manage Guild]: Permissions::MANAGE_GUILD
26

57struct NotSend;

59enum CacheRefInner<'a, K, V, T> {
60    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
61    Arc(Arc<V>),
62    DashRef(Ref<'a, K, V, BuildHasher>),
63    DashMappedRef(MappedRef<'a, K, T, V, BuildHasher>),
64    ReadGuard(parking_lot::RwLockReadGuard<'a, V>),
65}
66
67/// A reference to data in the [`Cache`].
68///
69/// This type wraps a reference to cached data and dereferences to `V`. It is deliberately marked
70/// `!Send` to prevent holding it across an `.await` point. Doing so can cause a deadlock: the
71/// underlying read lock is held for the lifetime of the `CacheRef`, so any task that tries taking
72/// the same lock while it is still held (i.e. across an `.await` point) will block indefinitely.
73///
74/// In general, the compiler will reject holding a `CacheRef` across an `.await` point in spawned
75/// tasks because it is `!Send`. Notably, however, the `#[tokio::main]` top-level future permits
76/// `.await`-ing `!Send` futures in its body. In this case the compiler will **not** prevent you
77/// from holding a `CacheRef` over an `.await` point, and a deadlock may still occur.
78///
79/// As a rule of thumb, never hold a `CacheRef` across an `.await` point. Instead, clone or copy the
80/// data you need and drop the reference before awaiting:
81///
82/// ```rust,no_run
83/// # use serenity::cache::Cache;
84/// # use serenity::model::prelude::*;
85/// # fn example(cache: &Cache, guild_id: GuildId) {
86/// // Good: extract what you need, then drop the reference.
87/// let channel_count = cache.guild(guild_id).map(|g| g.channels.len());
88/// # }
89/// ```
90pub struct CacheRef<'a, K, V, T = ()> {
91    inner: CacheRefInner<'a, K, V, T>,
92    phantom: std::marker::PhantomData<*const NotSend>,
93}
94
95impl<'a, K, V, T> CacheRef<'a, K, V, T> {
96    fn new(inner: CacheRefInner<'a, K, V, T>) -> Self {
97        Self {
98            inner,
99            phantom: std::marker::PhantomData,
100        }
101    }
102
103    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
104    fn from_arc(inner: MaybeOwnedArc<V>) -> Self {
105        Self::new(CacheRefInner::Arc(inner.get_inner()))
106    }
107
108    fn from_ref(inner: Ref<'a, K, V, BuildHasher>) -> Self {
109        Self::new(CacheRefInner::DashRef(inner))
110    }
111
112    fn from_mapped_ref(inner: MappedRef<'a, K, T, V, BuildHasher>) -> Self {
113        Self::new(CacheRefInner::DashMappedRef(inner))
114    }
115
116    fn from_guard(inner: parking_lot::RwLockReadGuard<'a, V>) -> Self {
117        Self::new(CacheRefInner::ReadGuard(inner))
118    }
119}
120
121impl<K: Eq + Hash, V, T> std::ops::Deref for CacheRef<'_, K, V, T> {
122    type Target = V;
123
124    fn deref(&self) -> &Self::Target {
125        match &self.inner {
126            #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
127            CacheRefInner::Arc(inner) => inner,
128            CacheRefInner::DashRef(inner) => inner.value(),
129            CacheRefInner::DashMappedRef(inner) => inner.value(),
130            CacheRefInner::ReadGuard(inner) => inner,
131        }
132    }
133}

158/// A cache containing data received from [`Shard`]s.
159///
160/// Using the cache allows to avoid REST API requests via the [`http`] module where possible.
161/// Issuing too many requests will lead to ratelimits.
162///
163/// This is the list of cached resources and the events that populate them:
164/// - channels: [`ChannelCreateEvent`], [`ChannelUpdateEvent`], [`GuildCreateEvent`]
165/// - guilds: [`GuildCreateEvent`]
166/// - unavailable_guilds: [`ReadyEvent`], [`GuildDeleteEvent`]
167/// - users: [`GuildMemberAddEvent`], [`GuildMemberRemoveEvent`], [`GuildMembersChunkEvent`],
168///   [`PresenceUpdateEvent`], [`ReadyEvent`]
169/// - presences: [`PresenceUpdateEvent`], [`ReadyEvent`]
170/// - messages: [`MessageCreateEvent`]
171///
172/// The documentation of each event contains the required gateway intents.
173///
174/// [`Shard`]: crate::gateway::Shard
175/// [`http`]: crate::http
176#[cfg_attr(feature = "typesize", derive(typesize::derive::TypeSize))]
177#[derive(Debug)]
178#[non_exhaustive]
179pub struct Cache {
180    // Temp cache:
181    // ---
182    /// Cache of channels that have been fetched via to_channel.
183    ///
184    /// The TTL for each value is configured in CacheSettings.
185    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
186    pub(crate) temp_channels: MokaCache<ChannelId, MaybeOwnedArc<GuildChannel>, BuildHasher>,
187    /// Cache of private channels created via create_dm_channel.
188    ///
189    /// The TTL for each value is configured in CacheSettings.
190    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
191    pub(crate) temp_private_channels: MokaCache<UserId, MaybeOwnedArc<PrivateChannel>, BuildHasher>,
192    /// Cache of messages that have been fetched via message.
193    ///
194    /// The TTL for each value is configured in CacheSettings.
195    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
196    pub(crate) temp_messages: MokaCache<MessageId, MaybeOwnedArc<Message>, BuildHasher>,
197    /// Cache of users who have been fetched from `to_user`.
198    ///
199    /// The TTL for each value is configured in CacheSettings.
200    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
201    pub(crate) temp_users: MokaCache<UserId, MaybeOwnedArc<User>, BuildHasher>,
202
203    // Channels cache:
204    /// A map of channel ids to the guilds in which the channel data is stored.
205    pub(crate) channels: MaybeMap<ChannelId, GuildId>,
206
207    // Guilds cache:
208    // ---
209    /// A map of guilds with full data available. This includes data like [`Role`]s and [`Emoji`]s
210    /// that are not available through the REST API.
211    pub(crate) guilds: MaybeMap<GuildId, Guild>,
212    /// A list of guilds which are "unavailable".
213    ///
214    /// Additionally, guilds are always unavailable for bot users when a Ready is received. Guilds
215    /// are "sent in" over time through the receiving of [`Event::GuildCreate`]s.
216    pub(crate) unavailable_guilds: MaybeMap<GuildId, ()>,
217
218    // Users cache:
219    // ---
220    /// A map of users that the current user sees.
221    ///
222    /// Users are added to - and updated from - this map via the following received events:
223    ///
224    /// - [`GuildMemberAdd`][`GuildMemberAddEvent`]
225    /// - [`GuildMemberRemove`][`GuildMemberRemoveEvent`]
226    /// - [`GuildMembersChunk`][`GuildMembersChunkEvent`]
227    /// - [`PresenceUpdate`][`PresenceUpdateEvent`]
228    /// - [`Ready`][`ReadyEvent`]
229    ///
230    /// Note, however, that users are _not_ removed from the map on removal events such as
231    /// [`GuildMemberRemove`][`GuildMemberRemoveEvent`], as other structs such as members or
232    /// recipients may still exist.
233    pub(crate) users: MaybeMap<UserId, User>,
234
235    // Messages cache:
236    // ---
237    pub(crate) messages: MessageCache,
238    /// Queue of message IDs for each channel.
239    ///
240    /// This is simply a vecdeque so we can keep track of the order of messages inserted into the
241    /// cache. When a maximum number of messages are in a channel's cache, we can pop the front and
242    /// remove that ID from the cache.
243    pub(crate) message_queue: DashMap<ChannelId, VecDeque<MessageId>, BuildHasher>,
244
245    // Miscellanous fixed-size data
246    // ---
247    /// Information about running shards
248    pub(crate) shard_data: RwLock<CachedShardData>,
249    /// The current user "logged in" and for which events are being received for.
250    ///
251    /// The current user contains information that a regular [`User`] does not, such as whether it
252    /// is a bot, whether the user is verified, etc.
253    ///
254    /// Refer to the documentation for [`CurrentUser`] for more information.
255    pub(crate) user: RwLock<CurrentUser>,
256    /// The settings for the cache.
257    settings: RwLock<Settings>,
258}

260impl Cache {
261    /// Creates a new cache.

263    #[must_use]
264    pub fn new() -> Self {
265        Self::default()
266    }

268    /// Creates a new cache instance with settings applied.
269    ///
270    /// # Examples
271    ///
272    /// ```rust
273    /// use serenity::cache::{Cache, Settings};
274    ///
275    /// let mut settings = Settings::default();
276    /// settings.max_messages = 10;
277    ///
278    /// let cache = Cache::new_with_settings(settings);
279    /// ```
280    #[instrument]
281    pub fn new_with_settings(settings: Settings) -> Self {
282        #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
283        fn temp_cache<K, V>(ttl: Duration) -> MokaCache<K, V, BuildHasher>
284        where
285            K: Hash + Eq + Send + Sync + 'static,
286            V: Clone + Send + Sync + 'static,
287        {
288            MokaCache::builder().time_to_live(ttl).build_with_hasher(BuildHasher::default())
289        }
290
291        Self {
292            #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
293            temp_private_channels: temp_cache(settings.time_to_live),
294            #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
295            temp_channels: temp_cache(settings.time_to_live),
296            #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
297            temp_messages: temp_cache(settings.time_to_live),
298            #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
299            temp_users: temp_cache(settings.time_to_live),
300
301            channels: MaybeMap(settings.cache_channels.then(DashMap::default)),
302
303            guilds: MaybeMap(settings.cache_guilds.then(DashMap::default)),
304            unavailable_guilds: MaybeMap(settings.cache_guilds.then(DashMap::default)),
305
306            users: MaybeMap(settings.cache_users.then(DashMap::default)),
307
308            messages: DashMap::default(),
309            message_queue: DashMap::default(),
310
311            shard_data: RwLock::new(CachedShardData {
312                total: 1,
313                connected: HashSet::new(),
314                has_sent_shards_ready: false,
315            }),
316            user: RwLock::new(CurrentUser::default()),
317            settings: RwLock::new(settings),
318        }
319    }
320
321    /// Fetches the number of [`Member`]s that have not had data received.
322    ///
323    /// The important detail to note here is that this is the number of _member_s that have not had
324    /// data received. A single [`User`] may have multiple associated member objects that have not
325    /// been received.
326    ///
327    /// This can be used in combination with [`Shard::chunk_guild`], and can be used to determine
328    /// how many members have not yet been received.
329    ///
330    /// ```rust,no_run
331    /// # use serenity::model::prelude::*;
332    /// # use serenity::prelude::*;
333    /// struct Handler;
334    ///
335    /// #[serenity::async_trait]
336    /// # #[cfg(feature = "client")]
337    /// impl EventHandler for Handler {
338    ///     async fn cache_ready(&self, ctx: Context, _: Vec<GuildId>) {
339    ///         println!("{} unknown members", ctx.cache.unknown_members());
340    ///     }
341    /// }
342    /// ```
343    ///
344    /// [`Shard::chunk_guild`]: crate::gateway::Shard::chunk_guild
345    pub fn unknown_members(&self) -> u64 {
346        let mut total = 0;
347
348        for guild_entry in self.guilds.iter() {
349            let guild = guild_entry.value();
350
351            let members = guild.members.len() as u64;
352
353            if guild.member_count > members {
354                total += guild.member_count - members;
355            }
356        }
357
358        total
359    }
360
361    /// Fetches a vector of all [`Guild`]s' Ids that are stored in the cache.
362    ///
363    /// Note that if you are utilizing multiple [`Shard`]s, then the guilds retrieved over all
364    /// shards are included in this count -- not just the current [`Context`]'s shard, if accessing
365    /// from one.
366    ///
367    /// # Examples
368    ///
369    /// Print all of the Ids of guilds in the Cache:
370    ///
371    /// ```rust,no_run
372    /// # use serenity::model::prelude::*;
373    /// # use serenity::prelude::*;
374    /// #
375    /// struct Handler;
376    ///
377    /// #[serenity::async_trait]
378    /// impl EventHandler for Handler {
379    ///     async fn ready(&self, context: Context, _: Ready) {
380    ///         let guilds = context.cache.guilds().len();
381    ///
382    ///         println!("Guilds in the Cache: {}", guilds);
383    ///     }
384    /// }
385    /// ```
386    ///
387    /// [`Context`]: crate::client::Context
388    /// [`Shard`]: crate::gateway::Shard
389    pub fn guilds(&self) -> Vec<GuildId> {
390        let unavailable_guilds = self.unavailable_guilds();
391
392        let unavailable_guild_ids = unavailable_guilds.iter().map(|i| *i.key());
393
394        self.guilds.iter().map(|i| *i.key()).chain(unavailable_guild_ids).collect()
395    }
396
397    /// Retrieves a [`GuildChannel`] from the cache based on the given Id.
398    #[inline]
399    #[deprecated = "Use Cache::guild and Guild::channels instead"]
400    pub fn channel<C: Into<ChannelId>>(&self, id: C) -> Option<GuildChannelRef<'_>> {
401        self.channel_(id.into())
402    }
403
404    fn channel_(&self, id: ChannelId) -> Option<GuildChannelRef<'_>> {
405        let guild_id = *self.channels.get(&id)?;
406        let guild_ref = self.guilds.get(&guild_id)?;
407        let channel = guild_ref.try_map(|g| g.channels.get(&id)).ok();
408        if let Some(channel) = channel {
409            return Some(CacheRef::from_mapped_ref(channel));
410        }
411
412        #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
413        {
414            if let Some(channel) = self.temp_channels.get(&id) {
415                return Some(CacheRef::from_arc(channel));
416            }
417        }
418
419        None
420    }

422    /// Get a reference to the cached messages for a channel based on the given `Id`.
423    ///
424    /// # Examples
425    ///
426    /// Find all messages by user ID 8 in channel ID 7:
427    ///
428    /// ```rust,no_run
429    /// # let cache: serenity::cache::Cache = todo!();
430    /// let messages_in_channel = cache.channel_messages(7);
431    /// let messages_by_user = messages_in_channel
432    ///     .as_ref()
433    ///     .map(|msgs| msgs.values().filter(|m| m.author.id == 8).collect::<Vec<_>>());
434    /// ```
435    pub fn channel_messages(
436        &self,
437        channel_id: impl Into<ChannelId>,
438    ) -> Option<ChannelMessagesRef<'_>> {
439        self.messages.get(&channel_id.into()).map(CacheRef::from_ref)
440    }

471    /// Retrieves a [`Guild`]'s member from the cache based on the guild's and user's given Ids.
472    ///
473    /// # Examples
474    ///
475    /// Retrieving the member object of the user that posted a message, in a
476    /// [`EventHandler::message`] context:
477    ///
478    /// ```rust,no_run
479    /// # use serenity::cache::Cache;
480    /// # use serenity::http::Http;
481    /// # use serenity::model::channel::Message;
482    /// #
483    /// # async fn run(http: Http, cache: Cache, message: Message) {
484    /// #
485    /// let roles_len = {
486    ///     let channel = match cache.channel(message.channel_id) {
487    ///         Some(channel) => channel,
488    ///         None => {
489    ///             if let Err(why) = message.channel_id.say(http, "Error finding channel data").await {
490    ///                 println!("Error sending message: {:?}", why);
491    ///             }
492    ///             return;
493    ///         },
494    ///     };
495    ///
496    ///     cache.member(channel.guild_id, message.author.id).map(|m| m.roles.len())
497    /// };
498    ///
499    /// let message_res = if let Some(roles_len) = roles_len {
500    ///     let msg = format!("You have {} roles", roles_len);
501    ///     message.channel_id.say(&http, &msg).await
502    /// } else {
503    ///     message.channel_id.say(&http, "Error finding member data").await
504    /// };
505    ///
506    /// if let Err(why) = message_res {
507    ///     println!("Error sending message: {:?}", why);
508    /// }
509    /// # }
510    /// ```
511    ///
512    /// [`EventHandler::message`]: crate::client::EventHandler::message
513    /// [`members`]: crate::model::guild::Guild::members
514    #[inline]
515    #[deprecated = "Use Cache::guild and Guild::members instead"]
516    pub fn member(
517        &self,
518        guild_id: impl Into<GuildId>,
519        user_id: impl Into<UserId>,
520    ) -> Option<MemberRef<'_>> {
521        self.member_(guild_id.into(), user_id.into())
522    }
523
524    fn member_(&self, guild_id: GuildId, user_id: UserId) -> Option<MemberRef<'_>> {
525        let member = self.guilds.get(&guild_id)?.try_map(|g| g.members.get(&user_id)).ok()?;
526        Some(CacheRef::from_mapped_ref(member))
527    }

529    #[inline]

531    pub fn guild_roles(&self, guild_id: impl Into<GuildId>) -> Option<GuildRolesRef<'_>> {
532        self.guild_roles_(guild_id.into())

535    fn guild_roles_(&self, guild_id: GuildId) -> Option<GuildRolesRef<'_>> {
536        let roles = self.guilds.get(&guild_id)?.map(|g| &g.roles);

569    /// Retrieves a [`Channel`]'s message from the cache based on the channel's and message's given
570    /// Ids.
571    ///
572    /// **Note**: This will clone the entire message.
573    ///
574    /// # Examples
575    ///
576    /// Retrieving the message object from a channel, in a [`EventHandler::message`] context:
577    ///
578    /// ```rust,no_run
579    /// # use serenity::cache::Cache;
580    /// # use serenity::model::channel::Message;
581    /// #
582    /// # fn run(cache: Cache, message: Message) {
583    /// #
584    /// match cache.message(message.channel_id, message.id) {
585    ///     Some(m) => assert_eq!(message.content, m.content),
586    ///     None => println!("No message found in cache."),
587    /// };
588    /// # }
589    /// ```
590    ///
591    /// [`EventHandler::message`]: crate::client::EventHandler::message
592    #[inline]
593    pub fn message<C, M>(&self, channel_id: C, message_id: M) -> Option<MessageRef<'_>>
594    where
595        C: Into<ChannelId>,
596        M: Into<MessageId>,
597    {
598        self.message_(channel_id.into(), message_id.into())
599    }
600
601    fn message_(&self, channel_id: ChannelId, message_id: MessageId) -> Option<MessageRef<'_>> {
602        #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
603        if let Some(message) = self.temp_messages.get(&message_id) {
604            return Some(CacheRef::from_arc(message));
605        }
606
607        let channel_messages = self.messages.get(&channel_id)?;
608        let message = channel_messages.try_map(|messages| messages.get(&message_id)).ok()?;
609        Some(CacheRef::from_mapped_ref(message))
610    }
611
612    /// Retrieves a [`Guild`]'s role by their Ids.
613    ///
614    /// **Note**: This will clone the entire role. Instead, retrieve the guild and retrieve from
615    /// the guild's [`roles`] map to avoid this.
616    ///
617    /// # Examples
618    ///
619    /// Retrieve a role from the cache and print its name:
620    ///
621    /// ```rust,no_run
622    /// # use serenity::cache::Cache;
623    /// #
624    /// # let cache = Cache::default();
625    /// // assuming the cache is in scope, e.g. via `Context`
626    /// if let Some(role) = cache.role(7, 77) {
627    ///     println!("Role with Id 77 is called {}", role.name);
628    /// };
629    /// ```
630    ///
631    /// [`Guild`]: crate::model::guild::Guild
632    /// [`roles`]: crate::model::guild::Guild::roles
633    #[inline]
634    #[deprecated = "Use Cache::guild and Guild::roles instead"]
635    pub fn role<G, R>(&self, guild_id: G, role_id: R) -> Option<GuildRoleRef<'_>>
636    where
637        G: Into<GuildId>,
638        R: Into<RoleId>,
639    {
640        self.role_(guild_id.into(), role_id.into())
641    }
642
643    fn role_(&self, guild_id: GuildId, role_id: RoleId) -> Option<GuildRoleRef<'_>> {
644        let role = self.guilds.get(&guild_id)?.try_map(|g| g.roles.get(&role_id)).ok()?;
645        Some(CacheRef::from_mapped_ref(role))
646    }
647
648    /// Returns the settings.
649    ///
650    /// # Examples
651    ///
652    /// Printing the maximum number of messages in a channel to be cached:
653    ///
654    /// ```rust
655    /// use serenity::cache::Cache;
656    ///
657    /// # fn test() {
658    /// let mut cache = Cache::new();
659    /// println!("Max settings: {}", cache.settings().max_messages);
660    /// # }
661    /// ```
662    pub fn settings(&self) -> SettingsRef<'_> {
663        CacheRef::from_guard(self.settings.read())
664    }
665
666    /// Sets the maximum amount of messages per channel to cache.
667    ///
668    /// By default, no messages will be cached.
669    pub fn set_max_messages(&self, max: usize) {
670        self.settings.write().max_messages = max;
671    }
672
673    /// Retrieves a [`User`] from the cache's [`Self::users`] map, if it exists.
674    ///
675    /// The only advantage of this method is that you can pass in anything that is indirectly a
676    /// [`UserId`].
677    ///
678    /// # Examples
679    ///
680    /// Retrieve a user from the cache and print their name:
681    ///
682    /// ```rust,no_run
683    /// # use serenity::client::Context;
684    /// #
685    /// # async fn test(context: &Context) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
686    /// if let Some(user) = context.cache.user(7) {
687    ///     println!("User with Id 7 is currently named {}", user.name);
688    /// }
689    /// # Ok(())
690    /// # }
691    /// ```
692    #[inline]
693    pub fn user<U: Into<UserId>>(&self, user_id: U) -> Option<UserRef<'_>> {
694        self.user_(user_id.into())
695    }
696
697    #[cfg(feature = "temp_cache")]
698    fn user_(&self, user_id: UserId) -> Option<UserRef<'_>> {
699        if let Some(user) = self.users.get(&user_id) {
700            Some(CacheRef::from_ref(user))
701        } else {
702            self.temp_users.get(&user_id).map(CacheRef::from_arc)
703        }
704    }
705
706    #[cfg(not(feature = "temp_cache"))]
707    fn user_(&self, user_id: UserId) -> Option<UserRef<'_>> {
708        self.users.get(&user_id).map(CacheRef::from_ref)
709    }
710
711    /// Clones all users and returns them.
712    #[inline]
713    pub fn users(&self) -> ReadOnlyMapRef<'_, UserId, User> {
714        self.users.as_read_only()
715    }
716
717    /// Returns the amount of cached users.
718    #[inline]
719    pub fn user_count(&self) -> usize {
720        self.users.len()
721    }
722
723    /// This method provides a reference to the user used by the bot.
724    #[inline]
725    pub fn current_user(&self) -> CurrentUserRef<'_> {
726        CacheRef::from_guard(self.user.read())
727    }
728
729    /// Returns a channel category matching the given ID
730    #[deprecated = "Use Cache::guild, Guild::channels, and GuildChannel::kind"]
731    pub fn category(&self, channel_id: ChannelId) -> Option<GuildChannelRef<'_>> {
732        #[allow(deprecated)]
733        let channel = self.channel(channel_id)?;
734        if channel.kind == ChannelType::Category {
735            Some(channel)
736        } else {
737            None
738        }
739    }
740
741    /// Returns the parent category of the given channel ID.
742    #[deprecated = "Use Cache::guild, Guild::channels, and GuildChannel::parent_id"]
743    pub fn channel_category_id(&self, channel_id: ChannelId) -> Option<ChannelId> {
744        #[allow(deprecated)]
745        self.channel(channel_id)?.parent_id
746    }
747
748    /// Clones all channel categories in the given guild and returns them.
749    pub fn guild_categories(&self, guild_id: GuildId) -> Option<HashMap<ChannelId, GuildChannel>> {
750        let guild = self.guilds.get(&guild_id)?;
751        Some(
752            guild
753                .channels
754                .iter()
755                .filter(|(_id, channel)| channel.kind == ChannelType::Category)
756                .map(|(id, channel)| (*id, channel.clone()))
757                .collect(),
758        )
759    }
760
761    /// Updates the cache with the update implementation for an event or other custom update
762    /// implementation.
763    ///
764    /// Refer to the documentation for [`CacheUpdate`] for more information.
765    ///
766    /// # Examples
767    ///
768    /// Refer to the [`CacheUpdate` examples].
769    ///
770    /// [`CacheUpdate` examples]: CacheUpdate#examples
771    #[instrument(skip(self, e))]
772    pub fn update<E: CacheUpdate>(&self, e: &mut E) -> Option<E::Output> {
773        e.update(self)
774    }
775
776    pub(crate) fn update_user_entry(&self, user: &User) {
777        if let Some(users) = &self.users.0 {
778            match users.entry(user.id) {
779                Entry::Vacant(e) => {
780                    e.insert(user.clone());
781                },
782                Entry::Occupied(mut e) => {
783                    e.get_mut().clone_from(user);
784                },
785            }
786        }
787    }
788}
789
790impl Default for Cache {
791    fn default() -> Self {
792        Self::new_with_settings(Settings::default())
793    }
794}
795
796#[cfg(test)]
797mod test {
798
799    use crate::cache::{Cache, CacheUpdate, Settings};
800    use crate::model::prelude::*;
801
802    #[test]
803    fn test_cache_messages() {
804        let settings = Settings {
805            max_messages: 2,
806            ..Default::default()
807        };
808        let cache = Cache::new_with_settings(settings);
809
810        // Test inserting one message into a channel's message cache.
811        let mut event = MessageCreateEvent {
812            message: Message {
813                id: MessageId::new(3),
814                guild_id: Some(GuildId::new(1)),
815                ..Default::default()
816            },
817        };
818
819        // Check that the channel cache doesn't exist.
820        assert!(!cache.messages.contains_key(&event.message.channel_id));
821        // Add first message, none because message ID 2 doesn't already exist.
822        assert!(event.update(&cache).is_none());
823        // None, it only returns the oldest message if the cache was already full.
824        assert!(event.update(&cache).is_none());
825        // Assert there's only 1 message in the channel's message cache.
826        assert_eq!(cache.messages.get(&event.message.channel_id).unwrap().len(), 1);
827
828        // Add a second message, assert that channel message cache length is 2.
829        event.message.id = MessageId::new(4);
830        assert!(event.update(&cache).is_none());
831        assert_eq!(cache.messages.get(&event.message.channel_id).unwrap().len(), 2);
832
833        // Add a third message, the first should now be removed.
834        event.message.id = MessageId::new(5);
835        assert!(event.update(&cache).is_some());
836
837        {
838            let channel = cache.messages.get(&event.message.channel_id).unwrap();
839
840            assert_eq!(channel.len(), 2);
841            // Check that the first message is now removed.
842            assert!(!channel.contains_key(&MessageId::new(3)));
843        }
844
845        let channel = GuildChannel {
846            id: event.message.channel_id,
847            guild_id: event.message.guild_id.unwrap(),
848            ..Default::default()
849        };
850
851        // Add a channel delete event to the cache, the cached messages for that channel should now
852        // be gone.
853        let mut delete = ChannelDeleteEvent {
854            channel: channel.clone(),
855        };
856        assert!(cache.update(&mut delete).is_some());
857        assert!(!cache.messages.contains_key(&delete.channel.id));
858
859        // Test deletion of a guild channel's message cache when a GuildDeleteEvent is received.
860        let mut guild_create = GuildCreateEvent {
861            guild: Guild {
862                id: GuildId::new(1),
863                channels: HashMap::from([(ChannelId::new(2), channel)]),
864                ..Default::default()
865            },
866        };
867        assert!(cache.update(&mut guild_create).is_none());
868        assert!(cache.update(&mut event).is_none());
869
870        let mut guild_delete = GuildDeleteEvent {
871            guild: UnavailableGuild {
872                id: GuildId::new(1),
873                unavailable: false,
874            },
875        };
876
877        // The guild existed in the cache, so the cache's guild is returned by the update.
878        assert!(cache.update(&mut guild_delete).is_some());
879
880        // Assert that the channel's message cache no longer exists.
881        assert!(!cache.messages.contains_key(&ChannelId::new(2)));
882    }
883}
